hypothesis: Quaternary fault scarps express in detrended topography as LINEAR breaks-in-slope (||grad det_elev_slope|| ridges with high structure-tensor coherence of det_elev). Faults that juxtapose like lithologies or offset only alluvium have a scarp but no magnetic/gravity contrast, so the H19-5 potential-field worm skeleton -- and with it parent R0 and the Qfaults-based catalogue built largely from mappable scarps on older imagery -- misses or misplaces them, while expert mapping on high-resolution DEMs (the competition label source, DrivenData #306 p.967) traces exactly such breaks. Placing 33-45% of the fixed budget on coherent slope-break ridges >3px off the worm skeleton, and keeping only coverage-nonredundant skeleton dots under the same field, raises expected kernel credit per dot versus R0's unranked geometric thinning.
mechanism: At fixed S=37,654, DTI rises when expected T gains outweigh denominator growth. Kept skeleton dots are chosen by exact marginal expected-DTI greedy (alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, triangular R=3px) under w=0.30+0.70*L_pct on H19-5 support, so coverage-redundant parent dots are the donors. Far dots take the strongest remaining coherent break lineaments first (descending L, 2.8px spacing floor): if per-pixel fault probability rises superlinearly with L rank -- as the screen's SGMC/catalogue enrichments indicated -- concentrating on the top lineaments at kernel spacing earns more expected credit per dot than spreading to cover low-rank support mass (measured directly: evidence/screen_vs_greedy_diagnostic.json).
